_meta.principle: APPEND-ONLY IN SPIRIT: shocks may be ADDED to `held_out_shocks` in a future edit, but an id already present here must NEVER be removed. Removing an id would retroactively invalidate every prior validation result computed against it (any reported accuracy/direction/calibration number implicitly assumed that shock was never trained on) -- there is no way to un-leak a shock after the fact, only to stop protecting it going forward, which defeats the point.
scope: No shock in `held_out_shocks` may appear as training data in any corpus (data/finetune/*.jsonl or any successor format), for any model, present or future.

No shock in `held_out_shocks` may be used to DERIVE a label (delta_bins/delta_eff/sentiment aggregate) that is then attached to a *different* (synthetic or real) training record -- this covers the thematic-grounding/sentiment-injection pathway in scripts/build_grounded_v2.py, not just direct use.

No shock in `held_out_shocks` may be used for hyperparameter tuning, model selection, or early-stopping decisions -- picking a checkpoint because it scores well on a held-out shock is the same violation as training on it directly.

This applies RETROACTIVELY: any existing artifact that already violates this (see the results of scripts/check_held_out_leakage.py logged in data/leakage_reports/) is a known, disclosed defect to be corrected in future corpus builds, not grandfathered in as acceptable.
This applies to every model version, past and future -- a shock is not held out 'for now,' it is held out permanently once listed here.
enforcement: electoral/data/held_out.py -- is_held_out()/assert_not_held_out()/assert_none_held_out(), the single source of truth read by all pipeline code
scripts/check_held_out_leakage.py -- standalone corpus scanner, direct AND indirect (thematic-grounding) leakage
_meta.selection_rationale_summary: 12 shocks are the docs/elicitation/ instrument's committed validation targets (must be held out or that ~6-week protocol is worthless). 4 more (afghanistan_withdrawal_2021, affirmative_action_scotus_2023, metoo_2017, chauvin_conviction_2021) were already being informally excluded via a hardcoded HELD_OUT_SOURCES constant in scripts/build_grounded_v2.py -- retained here to make that pre-existing, undocumented commitment canonical and enforced rather than silently walked back (see the leakage-check results: this walk-back had already partially happened once, between grounding-script v1 and v2). 4 more were added deliberately for ground-truth-layer and category coverage: trump_covid_diagnosis_2020 and election_2020 are the project's only Tier A (highest-fidelity, tightest-window) panel shocks worth dedicating to validation; trump_election_upset_2016 and election_2020 add exit-poll cross-cycle coverage; paris_climate_withdrawal_2017 fills the only major category (Environmental) otherwise absent from the set.
_meta.known_category_concentration: Electoral/Voting Rights accounts for 5 of 20 (dobbs_2022, jan_6_insurrection_2021, affirmative_action_scotus_2023, trump_election_upset_2016, election_2020) -- proportionate to how common that category is across all 56 configured shocks, not a design flaw, but noted for transparency rather than presented as a perfectly even split.
_meta.leakage_check_summary: 11 of 20 held-out shocks were found ALREADY LEAKED into existing corpora as of the freeze date (8 records direct, 609 records indirect via sentiment injection) -- see scripts/check_held_out_leakage.py and each affected shock's `leak_status` field below. NOT fixed as part of this freeze; disclosed as a known defect to correct in a future corpus rebuild. train.jsonl and eval.jsonl (the corpus actually used for the current production models, not the *_grounded_v2 variant) are CLEAN -- zero leaks found.

held_out_shocks.rationale: Predates every survey ground-truth layer (CES starts 2006, VOTER panel starts 2011) -- elicitation is the only validation this shock can ever get. Included in the 12-shock elicitation instrument as the rally-effect baseline.
Predates every survey ground-truth layer. Elicitation-only validation; the domestic (non-foreign-policy) incumbent-blame baseline with a racial-equity dimension in the elicitation set.

A constructed pilot scenario with no historical precedent -- no survey layer can ever cover it, and it cannot be 'looked up' by a model either, making it a clean reasoning-only test. Held out to keep the elicitation instrument's one novel-scenario item meaningful.
Straightforward incumbent-blame economic shock; CES year-pair (2007->2008) consistency check available. Elicitation set's economic-domain anchor.
Straightforward credit-to-incumbent shock, opposite valence from financial_crisis_2008. CES consistency check available.

The elicitation set's deliberate null/low-partisan-signal test case -- both parties broadly supported the same response, so this tests whether a model over-predicts partisan effects where none should exist. Held out so that test stays meaningful.

Panel data exists but its bracket window is too crowded (5 co-occurring shocks) for any statistical attribution -- elicitation is the ONLY usable validation this shock has at all. Highest-priority hold-out in the set for that reason alone.
Double-mobilization case (plausibly energized both pro-confirmation and #MeToo-aligned blocs). Panel Tier B consistency check available.
High-salience, emotionally direct shock; tests whether bloc-level predictions track general-polling disapproval or diverge from it. Panel Tier B consistency check available.
Double-mobilization case, different domain from kavanaugh_2018 (policing rather than judicial confirmation). Panel Tier B consistency check available.

The paradigmatic mobilizing-backlash case: a conservative-aligned legal outcome plausibly energizing the opposing coalition more than its own. Already excluded via the pre-existing (undocumented) HELD_OUT_SOURCES constant in scripts/build_grounded_v2.py -- now made canonical.
Sharply divergent contemporaneous partisan interpretation of the same event. CES consistency check available.

Already excluded via the pre-existing (undocumented) HELD_OUT_SOURCES constant in scripts/build_grounded_v2.py -- retained here to make that prior commitment canonical and enforced rather than allow it to lapse the way blm_george_floyd_2020's and kavanaugh_2018's earlier (v1-script) exclusions did.
Already excluded via the pre-existing (undocumented) HELD_OUT_SOURCES constant in scripts/build_grounded_v2.py -- retained here to make that prior commitment canonical and enforced.

Already excluded via the pre-existing (undocumented) HELD_OUT_SOURCES constant in scripts/build_grounded_v2.py -- retained here to make that prior commitment canonical and enforced. Also a panel Tier C (statistically unusable) shock in its own right.
Already excluded via the pre-existing (undocumented) HELD_OUT_SOURCES constant in scripts/build_grounded_v2.py -- retained here to make that prior commitment canonical and enforced.

One of only two Tier A (highest-fidelity, 46-day-window) panel shocks in the entire ground-truth set -- deliberately dedicated to validation rather than training. Also the only Health/Pandemic-category shock in this held-out set, filling a category gap the elicitation-12 didn't cover. Shares its panel bracket window with election_2020 and ruth_bader_ginsburg_2020 (see data/ground_truth/panel_deltas_summary.md); ruth_bader_ginsburg_2020 was deliberately left trainable to avoid over-holding-out from one narrow shared window.
Fills the Environmental category, otherwise entirely absent from this held-out set. Panel Tier B consistency check available.

Adds exit-poll cross-cycle coverage (the 2004->2016 comparison) to the held-out set, which otherwise skews toward panel/CES. One of the most consequential single election shocks in the taxonomy; a genuine 'surprise' mobilizing-dynamics test case.

The single richest ground-truth shock in the whole project -- Tier A panel data AND its own exit-poll cycle delta (2016->2020) in one shock, enabling a genuine cross-layer agreement check restricted to properly held-out data (data/ground_truth/ground_truth_layers.md already found panel and exit-poll disagree in sign for 5/6 blocs on this exact comparison -- validating against BOTH, honestly, requires this shock never be trained on).
